rationale: Ground truth's substantive content boils down to one real actionable point (david6666666's suggestion to dedupe with module_collector.py's existing attrgetter-based resolver); Y hits this almost exactly by proposing returning (name, module) tuples to enable id(module) dedup like module_collector.py does, and separately echoes the same file's warning-on-failure pattern for the silent except-AttributeError branch — X only gestures at the inconsistency and asks an open question about unifying consumers. Both candidates independently converge on a genuine, well-grounded SoulX Singer risk, but Y substantiates it with concrete sequence-length/DBCache mechanics while X's version is comparatively shallow. Y's findings are also more concretely actionable (exact log messages, code diffs, specific test additions) versus X's more hedged 'could you confirm' framing, making Y the clearly stronger review despite similar overall groundedness.
